questions.question: Critically examine the core philosophical foundations and values of social work. How do these influence ethical practice in real-world settings?
questions.solution_html:
• Critically examine the core philosophical foundations and values of social work.
  • How do these influence ethical practice in real-world settings?
  • i) Social work is rooted in human rights, social justice, dignity, and the worth of
  • every individual. Philosophically, it draws on principles from deontology (duty-
  • based ethics), utilitarianism (maximizing well-being), and virtue ethics
  • (character and moral integrity). These values promote client-centered care,
  • advocacy for the oppressed, and professional integrity.
  • ii) In real-world settings, these principles guide decisions on issues such as resource
  • allocation, advocacy, confidentiality, and client autonomy. For example, a social
  • worker may have to balance institutional rules with the ethical obligation to advocate
  • for a homeless client’s right to housing, even if that means challenging the status quo.
  • These foundations ensure ethical consistency while addressing complex, real-life
  • challenges.
questions.final_answer: Verified solution per MGU Scheme of Valuation.

questions.question: Evaluate the importance of maintaining competence for delivering effective and responsible social services
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the importance of maintaining competence for delivering effective and
  • responsible social services
  • i. Competence is a core ethical obligation and critical to providing high-quality,
  • evidence-informed services. Social work constantly evolves with new laws,
  • research, and client needs. Without ongoing education and training, a social
  • worker risks using outdated methods, misinterpreting cultural contexts, or
  • violating legal and ethical standards.
  • ii. a) Maintaining competence ensures accountability, promotes client trust, and
  • aligns practice with the profession’s ethical code.
  • b) It also enables innovation in interventions and enhances interprofessional
  • collaboration, especially in fields like mental health, child protection, or
  • disability services.
questions.final_answer: Verified per official MGU Scheme of Valuation.

questions.question: Explain the principles of social work
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the principles of social work
  • a) Acceptance – Accepting clients without judgment.
  • b) Individualization – Recognizing each client’s uniqueness.
  • c) Self-determination – Respecting clients’ right to make decisions.
  • d) Confidentiality – Protecting client information.
  • e) Non-judgmental attitude – Avoiding bias and prejudice.
  • f) Controlled emotional involvement – Maintaining professional balance.
  • g) Purposeful expression of feelings – Allowing clients to express emotions.
  • h) Professional relationship – Building trust and respect.
  • i) Accountability – Being responsible for professional actions.
  • j) Social justice – Promoting fairness and equality in society.
questions.final_answer: j) Social justice – Promoting fairness and equality in society.

questions.question: Evaluate the ethical strengths and challenges of applying philosophical values in community practice
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the ethical strengths and challenges of applying philosophical values in
  • community practice
  • • Philosophical values like social justice and community empowerment
  • inspire inclusive practices, participatory decision-making, and advocacy for
  • marginalized groups.
  • • They provide a moral compass that helps social workers navigate competing
  • interests and advocate for systemic change.
  • Challenges:
  • • Real-world constraints, such as political agendas, funding limitations, or
  • community resistance, may conflict with these ideals.
  • • Balancing individual rights with community needs can create ethical
  • tensions (e.g., advocating for needle exchange programs that face public
  • opposition).
  • Ultimately, applying philosophical values in community work requires critical
  • reflection, ethical dialogue, and strategic advocacy to remain effective and
  • accountable.
questions.final_answer: Verified per official MGU Scheme of Valuation.

questions.question: Critically evaluate the ethical principles embedded in Rights-Based and Developmental models.
questions.solution_html:
• Critically evaluate the ethical principles embedded in Rights-Based and Developmental models
  • a) Rights-Based model emphasizes human rights, equality, and justice.
  • b) Promotes empowerment and participation of marginalized groups.
  • c) Ensures accountability of institutions and governments.
  • d) Risk: May be difficult to implement in resource-poor settings.
  • e) Sometimes leads to conflict with cultural norms.
  • f) Developmental model focuses on growth, capacity-building, and sustainability.
  • g) Encourages self-reliance and long-term solutions.
  • h) Risk: May overlook immediate needs of vulnerable populations.
  • i) Ethical strength: Balances individual and community development.
  • j) Both models complement each other—ethical practice requires integrating rights protection with
  • sustainable development
questions.final_answer: Verified solution per MGU Scheme of Valuation.
